speaker: Doctor

text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any yellowing of your skin or eyes, and has your stool become pale or clay-colored? I also need to know if you have experienced any itching or joint pain recently.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mild scleral icterus observed. Liver palpated 2–3 cm below the right costal margin, tender on palpation. Liver Function Panel results: Total Bilirubin 3.6 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin 2.4 mg/dL, Alkaline Phosphatase 72 U/L, AST 488 U/L, ALT 798 U/L.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent exposure to unknown foods at the fair and the marked elevation in AST and ALT, have you noticed any dark, tarry stools or experienced vomiting? I will also check for jaundice and abdominal tenderness more thoroughly. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hepatitis A IgG Antibody: Positive, Hepatitis B Surface Antigen: Positive, Hepatitis B Core IgG Antibody: Positive, Hepatitis B Envelope Antigen: Positive, Hepatitis C Antibody: Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of Hepatitis B Surface Antigen and Envelope Antigen confirms an acute Hepatitis B infection. Do you have any history of unprotected sexual contact, IV drug use, or recent tattoos that could explain the transmission? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_B_Viral_Load

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal viral load result seems inconsistent with the other markers indicating active infection, so I need to clarify the clinical picture. Have you ever received the Hepatitis B vaccine in the past, and do you have any history of chronic liver disease? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_B_DNA

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal HBV DNA and HBsAg/HBeAg positivity suggest an inactive carrier state or assay interference, making Hepatitis A the likely acute cause given the IgG positivity and food exposure. I will request imaging to assess liver morphology and rule out other causes of the elevated enzymes. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Social history: Consumes 1–2 beers daily. Works as a nursing assistant in a rehabilitation facility.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal HBV DNA and positive Hepatitis A IgG, the Hepatitis B markers likely represent chronic inactive carriage or false positives, while the acute symptoms align with Hepatitis A exposure. I have sufficient evidence to conclude that the patient is suffering from acute Hepatitis A infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis A
